written: 2026-10-12, committed before any hour of the sizing week was streamed and before any pull request was fetched
what: The sizing run for sealed-ahead precision (study 2026-10-06, section 2.1 and section 4 step 4): one past week of GH Archive through the builder's population.py and pool.py, then a uniform sample of at most 300 admitted records through the builder's accuse.py and the frozen 7.49.0 gate. Counts only: no adjudication, no precision, and no table by repository, account or product. Agent family appears only as a sizing count of admitted records.

gate.package_source: git -c core.autocrlf=false archive v7.49.0 styxx, extracted to sizing_derived/styxx_7_49_0 (not committed); accuse.load_gate refuses any other diffgate
gate.call: gate_diff_text(title + "\n\n" + body, diff, run=None, strict=False), as accuse.gate_outcome makes it
gate.interpreter: py -3.12 (CPython 3.12.10 on this machine); the run records interpreter and unicodedata version

provisional_params.note: Not a plan. These fill the builder's parameter schema for one sizing run. account_id_ceiling and repo_id_ceiling are derived by `sizing.py ceilings` from the calibration hour named by young_days (pool.py ceilings' rule); bitcoin_height is a placeholder because the sizing run draws nothing.

age_rule_sensitivity.what: The same week counted again, before deduplication, under the age rule at other young_days and with no age rule. Counts only; the pool and the sample use the provisional params above.

sample.frame: pool.jsonl as pool.assemble writes it under the provisional params (one record per (repo_id, number), uncapped)
sample.seed: styxx sealed-ahead sizing week 2026-09-28 sample v0
sample.method: for each record, key = sha256(canon({"pool_key": "<repo_id>#<number>", "seed": seed})) as lowercase hex, canon being common.canon; the n_max records with the smallest keys form the sample (all records if the pool holds fewer); the sample is then ordered by event id as accuse.run orders it
sample.why_this_method: A pure function of the seed and the pool: anyone holding the pool re-derives the sample, and the seed is fixed here before the pool exists, so it cannot be chosen to suit the sample.

fetch_budget.routes: accuse.py's own: api.github.com/repositories/<repo_id>/pulls/<number>, then github.com/<owner>/<name>/pull/<number>.diff; unauthenticated; no other GitHub request is made
fetch_budget.limiter: accuse.RateLimiter with its stamps kept in the output directory
fetch_budget.if_the_budget_runs_out: the records without a final outcome are reported as unfetched, with the partial counts and the method; nothing is extrapolated over them

estimators.denominator: sampled records with a final outcome (admitted agent pull requests, whatever their outcome: HEAD_MOVED, EMPTY_BODY and PR_GONE records count in the denominator because the window's population holds them too); the rate per gated record is reported beside it
estimators.per_kind: accusations of each kind per 1,000 sampled records; Wilson 95% interval on the share of sampled records with at least one accusation of that kind (z = 1.959964), and the same for any kind
estimators.projection: admitted records in the week times the sampled rate, at the point estimate and at both Wilson ends
estimators.window_for_60: 60 divided by the weekly projection at the Wilson lower end, in days; unbounded when the lower end is zero. The fetch budget is a second limit and is computed from the sample's measured requests per record
estimators.not_computed: precision, any accusation count by family, repository, account or product
